content:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert — Escalation policy "prod-critical" fired for service "inference-runtime". Incident PD-45678. Primary on-call (alice) did not acknowledge within 2m; auto-escalating to secondary and manager. https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-45678

pagerduty-bot: PD: Incident PD-45678 triggered by check "inference:latency_p95">1200ms. Escalation path: primary -> secondary (bob) -> manager (carol). Escalation stage: 1/3. Auto-escalation in 3m if unacked.

alice: ack — joining bridge. seeing a big spike in token generation latencies. :rotating_light:

alice: quick summary: queues backing up on host gpu-rt-4, OOMs from worker-3. collecting logs now.

bob: i also got paged. pulling kube events and pod logs. any recent deploys?

pagerduty-bot: PD: primary did ack at 1934567925 (delay 35s). Escalation halted.

carol: i was paged due to escalation policy. available if manager-level escalation needed.

dave: if pods are OOMing, could be a bad model load or a memory leak. any config changes in last 30m?

alice: no deploys. looks like telemetry ingestion surge from customers A/B — autoscaler thrashing and then pods OOMing.

bob: restarting inference-worker-3 to reclaim memory. will cordon node gpu-rt-4 if it recurs.

alice: running restart now:
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/inference-worker -n prod --selector=app=inference-worker
```

bob: restarted; logs show OOM count dropping. p95 latency falling from ~1.8s -> ~700ms.

pagerduty-bot: PD: Auto-escalation timer expired for secondary; manager notified at 1934568010 (PD-45678).

carol: standing by. please prepare a short timeline for support/cs to notify customers if needed.

alice: sending note to support: short degradation ~17m, increased retries, partial failures for heavy-usage customers; mitigation started (pod restarts / autoscaler throttling).

alice: silencing noisy alert for 30m while we stabilize:
```
pagerduty incidents silence PD-45678 --duration 30m
```

alice: handing off to matt in ~12m. leaving notes:
- cause: ingestion spike -> autoscaler thrash -> pod OOMs
- mitigations taken: restart worker pods, throttle autoscaler, cordon node if repeat
- watch: p95 latency < 800ms, error-rate < 0.5%
- PD incident id PD-45678

matt: ack. i'll take watch and follow up on metrics/alerts. :thumbsup:

bob: adding temporary autoscaler stability by patching HPA behavior:
```
kubectl patch hpa inference-worker -n prod --type='json' -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/behavior","value":{"scaleDown":{"stabilizationWindowSeconds":600}}}]'
```

alice: thanks. monitoring dashboards show improved tail latency. will keep the incident in monitoring state and update when we close.

incident-bot: PD-45678 status: monitoring. last update 1934568200. :white_check_mark:
